newsitem.title: UK: Brady debt mixed, Brazil down on bribe allegations.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt mixed, Brazil down on bribe allegations.

text.p: Brady bond prices were mixed on Wednesday as market participants awaited key U.S. inflation data but emerging market debt traders said much of the attention remained on corruption allegations in Brazil.

"There are continued rumblings about corruption in Brazil but there are no specific details. It's just a fact that there may be corruption in what was thought to be a corruption free government but I cannot speculate what that may mean for the future," said one trader at a U.S. investment bank in London.
Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR continued their downward slide, falling 5/8 to 75-5/8 bid from New York's one percentage point drop on Tuesday from 76-1/4 bid.

Sharp declines in Brazilian Brady debt were attributed to a local Brazilian newspaper report which alleged five congressmen took bribes to vote in favour of a bill that would allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for re-election. A Presidential spokesman for President Cardoso said on Tuesday the corruption scandal in Congress would be investigated but it would not affect the progress of the bill that would allow Cardoso to run for a second term.
Still, emerging market experts said the scandal could delay re-election and administrative reforms.

"This sort of bribe scandal does not look good, so presumably admininistrative reform and the re-election (bill) will be delayed because of this," another trader at a U.S. investment bank in London said. The trader noted that Brazilian Bradies were lower as market players sought to diversify their holdings by moving cash out of Brazil into Mexico, Panama, Argentina and Bulgaria.

"There is more diversification away from Brazil in this environment," he said. Indeed, Bulgaria enjoyed mild price gains, with its IABs BGFLTH11=RR up 3/8 at 66-3/8 bid and its discount bonds BGFLTH24A up 1/4 at 67-3/8. Bulgarian Bradies, which have risen by more than 50 percent this year, are expected to continue to outshine the broader emerging debt market. "Bulgaria will continue to outperform the market in expectation that the government will successfully implement the reform program they have designed in conjunction with the IMF (International Monetary Fund)," said David Boren, vice president of economic and market analysis at Salomon Brothers in London.

Boren also said expectations that the currency board will be implemented in July and that the Brady payment will made at the end of July should add to the positive tone for Bulgaria. Elsewhere, Russian Vneshekonombank dollar-denominated loans RUVNUSLNS=RR rose 3/8 to 84-1/8 bid following news that NATO had reached an agreement with Russia on a new relationship. In the broader market, Agrentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR eased 1/8 lower to 92-1/4 bid, while Mexican pars MX625L19=RR firmed 1/8 stronger to 74 bid and Panamanian PDI's PAPDI=RR were unchanged at 86-1/8 bid. --Diane Craft, London Newsroom +44 171 542 5110
